subject: Re: GreenWave AWS Marketplace private offer — buyer approvals & term options
messages:
From: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@greenwave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenwave.com
Date: 2028-07-11 08:12 -0700
Subject: AWS private offer — procurement questions and preferred term

Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is starting the internal review of the AWS Marketplace private offer. Two asks from our side before we loop in finance: any guidance on recommended term length (12 vs 24 months) tied to activation discounts, and what buyer approvals we should expect on our end to get a private offer fully approved in AWS?

High level context: GreenWave is evaluating a 100k annual commit (usage-based) for your inference hosted offering, with a potential expansion to reserved capacity in year two if performance/latency meet our SLAs. We want to make sure the private offer in AWS maps to our procurement gates so the signing window isn't blocked by procurement/finance.

Can you share a short checklist of internal buyer approvers (who signs what) and whether a 12-month term with a ramp option is feasible? We also need any evidence pack (SOC2, data residency) to attach to our procurement ticket.

Thanks,
Laura Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager
GreenWave Energy

Attachment: GreenWave_PO_Request.docx (stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@greenwave.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11 09:15 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — procurement questions and preferred term

Laura — appreciate the clear ask and context. High level answers first, then proposed next steps: 

1) Recommended term length: our standard private-offer play for pilots is 12 months with a 30–60 day ramp clause. For enterprise activation we often see buyers choose 12 + optional auto-renew or 24 months in exchange for an additional 8–12% activation rebate. If GreenWave expects to move to dedicated/reserved capacity in year two, we can structure a performance-triggered credit that flows back into year-two committed pricing.

2) Buyer approvals: typical buyer signoff path for MW/enterprise customers on AWS private offers: procurement approval (procurement lead), legal (counterparty T&Cs), finance (budget owner / CFO delegate) and AWS Marketplace admin (to accept and activate the private offer). On our side, sales + finance must counter-sign the private offer and we run a brief legal review for any non-standard terms.

3) Evidence: we can attach our SOC 2 report, data residency clauses, and an operations runbook. I will follow up with Neha (security/compliance) to drop the latest SOC2 and a short evidence pack.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll put together a suggested private-offer structure (term, credit schedule, acceptance window) and an approvals checklist by tomorrow EOD.
- Vanessa, can you confirm the maximum activation rebate range we can offer for a 24-month commitment?
- Karthik, flag anything legal that would block a performance-triggered credit structure.

Laura — after we align internally I’ll send a doc + an annotated AWS PoD (private-offer document) that your procurement team can attach to the ticket.

Best,
Marcus
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@greenwave.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-11 11:03 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — procurement questions and preferred term

Quick note on rebate/credit structure:
- 12 month term: standard activation credit 0%–4% depending on seat/usage mix (not typical for pure usage).
- 24 month term: we can layer a 6%–12% one-time activation rebate applied as a bill credit across the first 3 months of activation; we prefer to avoid multi-year negative cash impact so rebate is structured as a credit, not a prepaid discount.

Performance-triggered credit: acceptable if we bind KPIs concretely (p95 latency threshold, avg token cost target, activation by X date). Legal will want objective, measurable gates and a defined remediation path (fallback model variant / rate card until SLA satisfied).

Approver checklist (what you’ll need on GreenWave side):
- Procurement owner name + procurement ticket ID
- Legal contact for contract redlines (name/email)
- Finance owner (budget approver / person who signs POs)
- AWS Marketplace admin who will accept/activate the private offer (must have AWS console access)

I’ll attach an approvals matrix and a sample credit schedule. Marcus — we should offer the 12-month with optional 12-month extension option in the PoD and list the 24-month as a negotiated alternative with the wider rebate band.

Attachment: approval_matrix.xlsx (stub)

-Vanessa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@greenwave.com>
Date: 2028-07-12 09:04 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS private offer — procurement questions and preferred term

Laura / team — legal notes on performance-triggered credit:
- We can accept a credit tied to measurable activation KPIs, but we need:
  * Clear KPI definitions (metric, measurement window, tooling/source of truth)
  * A remediation escalation ladder (30-day cure, model fallback, billing at standard rate until resolved)
  * Limit on aggregate credit exposure (e.g., capped at X% of ARR or $Y)

- Redlines: cannot agree to open-ended financial make-goods. We’ll propose a cap (suggest 10% of first-year committed spend) and a defined window to evaluate.

I’ve attached a redline checklist and flagged the clauses I’ll need GreenWave legal to confirm. If they require a full contract change, it will add ~5 business days. For the AWS private offer itself, the activation window should be 30 days from signing to avoid stale offers in Marketplace.

-Karthik

Attachment: legal_redline_checklist.txt (stub)

2) Our AWS admin (tom.hart@greenwave.com) will be the activator; I’ve added him to the procurement ticket.
3) Please send the evidence pack (SOC2, runbook) and the annotated PoD. If you can include the proposed credit cap number in the PoD we can move to legal review this week.

Laura
